query: Which pre-registered event windows (intraday minutes, 1-3 day, 7-14 day) balance statistical power and protection against ECB reaction-to-market reverse causality?

response.query: Which pre-registered event windows (intraday minutes, 1-3 day, 7-14 day) balance statistical power and protection against ECB reaction-to-market reverse causality?
response.answer: Pre-ECB event windows balance statistical power and protection against reverse causality by focusing on intraday minutes and 1-3 day windows. The 7-14 day window may dilute effects. Short windows capture immediate market reactions.

results.title: The Euro Area Monetary Policy Event-Study Database | CEPR
results.content: # The Euro Area Monetary Policy Event-Study Database. This column introduces a new database, the Euro Area Monetary Policy Event-Study Database, which makes available intraday asset price changes around ECB policy announcements for a wide range of assets. The high resolution of the intraday data allows for the measurement of asset price changes separately for the press release and press conference windows. The event-study literature provides identified effects of monetary policy by looking at high frequency (daily or higher frequency) asset price changes around the policy announcement, with the identifying assumption that within the day monetary policy does not react to asset prices, and therefore causality goes from monetary policy to asset prices. The event-study literature on monetary policy effects on asset prices in the US goes back to Cook and Hahn (1988) and has flourished after Kuttner (2001) showed how to use Federal Funds Futures contracts to measure market perceived monetary policy surprises. The common theme among these papers, other than their event study-based research design, is the need to construct databases of high frequency asset price changes around policy announcements. This column explains the contents of the Euro Area Monetary Policy Event-Study Database (EA-MPD), which presents intraday asset price changes for the history of ECB Governing Council announcements, and will be kept updated by the authors. Using fine intraday data, we measure asset price changes for the Press Release Window, the Press Conference Window, and their union, the Monetary Event Window. Figure 3 shows the changes in the OIS yield curve in the two event windows for these four policy dates. The OIS rate changes at different maturities presented in this figure are taken directly from the EA-MPD, which contains this data, and more, for all policy dates. We have used this database to extract market-implied latent factors that drive yield curve changes on policy days and found that monetary policy communication in the euro area has always been multi-faceted, that a single ‘communication’ measure was never sufficient to capture the market reaction in the Press Conference window (Altavilla et al. Altavilla, C, L Brugnolini, R Gürkaynak, R Motto, and G Ragusa (2019b), "Monetary policy in action: Multiple dimensions of ECB policy communication and their financial market effects", VoxEU.org, 4 October.

results.title: Uncovering the Pre-ECB Drift and Its Trading Strategy Applications - QuantPedia
results.content: Our quantitative analysis reveals that European equity markets tend to exhibit a strong and consistent upward drift on the day *before* the ECB’s scheduled press conference. In central banking, the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Federal Reserve (FED) play pivotal roles in shaping financial markets through their monetary policies. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting effect, as documented by Quantpedia meeting effect, as documented by Quantpedia"), highlights significant stock price movements around FOMC announcements, underscoring the impact of central bank decisions on financial markets. Preliminary findings indicate that markets exhibit significant drift and volatility adjustments preceding ECB policy decisions, which differ slightly from the price-action around FED announcements. Let’s continue and and study the performance of D-1 equity curves, highlighting the effectiveness of holding European stock indices D-1 days before ECB meetings. We can observe that the pre-ECB drift occurs during 3 different sessions – Close-to-Open session during the night (from D-2 to D-1), then during the Open-to-Close session in the D-1, and indexes have a still positive performance during the Close-to-Open session from D-1 to D0 day (so during the night preceding ECB press-conference). The equity curves for D0 Open-to-Close sessions in both indices reveal an adverse market reaction to ECB announcements, indicating that markets tend to react negatively to ECB policy revelations. You must sell them on D-1 close as the ECB rate decision is announced on D0 day in the morning when the US market is still closed. The most probable explanation is that US institutional investors front-run the announcement and unwind their longs the day before the meeting at the close of the US session since the ECB announcement release is scheduled in pre-market hours, outside of the regular trading session in America. The distribution of the performance for days D-3 to D+3 for the spread itself should give us some understanding of whether the pre-ECB drift is caused by the performance of the global stock markets or just by the European price action itself. Investors can develop more informed strategies to capitalize on market movements around ECB policy announcements by identifying and quantifying the pre-ECB effect.
